problem: Prior navigation policies are trained on a single goal modality (egocentric image, 2D pose, or language), which limits usable datasets, test-time flexibility, and cross-modal representation learning.
motivation: Humans combine language, GPS/coordinates and visual landmarks when navigating, and these modalities are complementary. Robot navigation data is scattered across datasets that each carry only some modalities, so a model that ingests any subset could exploit far more data and become a more flexible foundation model.
key_idea: Fine-tune a large VLA (OpenVLA with an OFT action head) on ~9,500 hours of navigation data with randomized goal-modality dropout and masking, so one policy accepts language, 2D pose, goal image, or combinations of them.
insight: Joint multi-modal training beats single-modality training on the same architecture: in the OmniVLA-edge ablation, language rises from 0.43 to 0.60 and satellite-image goals from 0.19 to 0.57. The large VLM/VLA backbone matters most for language and OOD behavior following: OmniVLA-edge reaches 0.25 Behavior versus 0.65 for OmniVLA, and the small MiniVLA/SmolVLA backbones perform poorly. Adding BDD-V driving data recovers roughly half of the failures of the model trained without it.
method: Backbone: OpenVLA (7B, Llama2 + DINOv2/SigLIP) with a linear action head (OpenVLA-OFT) that outputs N=8 actions at 3 Hz; trained with LoRA (~5% of parameters).
Goal encoders: a visual backbone and projector for goal images and a projector for 2D goal poses map each goal modality into the shared LLM token space, and the language prompt is fed as text.

Randomized modality fusion: for each sample a goal modality subset t_m is drawn from those available in the dataset; unused modalities are filled with random values and excluded through an attention mask (modality dropout in training, masking at inference).

Data mixture: 13 public datasets (GNM, LeLaN, Frodobots-2K, BDD-V) totalling 9,500 hours over 10 platforms, sampled LeLaN:GNM:Frodobots:BDD-V = 4:1:1:1; synthetic actions come from MBRA/NoMaD, and a customized MBRA reannotation model handles the BDD-V embodiment gap.
Objective: an MSE imitation loss J_il on the action chunk, plus a LeLaN-only object-reaching loss (last action close to the target object pose) and an action-smoothness loss.

OmniVLA-edge: a 50M ViNT-based variant with EfficientNet-B0 and CLIP+FiLM language conditioning, plus a pose projector, early fusion and the same modality masking, for resource-constrained deployment.
Deployment: topological graph for long-range image goals; GPS-derived relative goal pose for pose goals; velocity commands sent to the robot.

setting.backbone: OpenVLA 7B (Llama2-7B + DINOv2+SigLIP, LoRA fine-tuned); also OmniVLA-edge (ViNT-based, 50M), MiniVLA 1B, SmolVLA 500M
setting.training_data: ~9,500 hours across 10 platforms: GNM mixture (62 h), LeLaN mixture (128.7 h, synthetic language and actions), Frodobots-2K (700 h, MBRA relabeled), BDD-V (8680 h, reannotated); OpenVLA pre-training inherited
setting.observation: monocular front RGB camera (current image, plus goal image), GPS-based 2D goal pose, language prompt
setting.action_space: predicted action chunk of 8 waypoints at 3 Hz, converted to linear/angular velocity commands
setting.privileged: none (GPS used for pose goals; topological map of prior images for image goals)

numbers.extra: real-world trials in 40 environments; SR^S = simple, SR^C = with obstacles; Behavior = OOD prompt following

numbers_note: All evaluation is on the authors' own real-world trials, not standard benchmarks; success rates are printed as fractions (0-1). Number of trials for some tasks is not fully stated.
results: OmniVLA outperforms specialist baselines: language SR 0.73 vs 0.43 (LeLaN), pose SR 0.95 vs 0.86 (MBRA-pose), and image SR 1.00, matching MBRA-image. It achieves 0.80 SR on the pose+language composition where NoMaD reaches 0.40 and MBRA-pose 0.70. Fine-tuning on CounterfactualVLA data raises SR to 0.825 and Behavior to 0.700.
limitations: Language-conditioned navigation still has room for improvement in goal-reaching and instruction-following; it needs larger, better-curated language datasets.
Evaluation is real-world only on small trial counts, with no standard simulated benchmarks; the 7B model is too heavy for resource-constrained deployment and is run remotely over the internet.
Synthetic and re-annotated labels (LeLaN, MBRA) can be noisy.
